# robotstxt example: MU bulleting

In the chunk below, we used the robotstxt package to check if we are allowed to write a program that scrapes the page: https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/.

```{r}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "courses-instruction/isa/",
  domain="https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/"
)
```

Returns TRUE --> we are allowed to scrape it



# robotstxt: Wikipedia

```{r}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/wiki/", domain = "https://en.wikipedia.org"
    )
```

FALSE --> can't use it




# robotstxt: Linkedin

```{r}
# In some cases, the robotstxt provides inconsistent answers
# typically, you get a warning with the answer that is incorrect
# solution: drop the trailing slash from the URL
# even better check with the robots.txt (which is the ground truth)
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/jobs/", domain = "www.linkedin.com"
    )
```

FALSE --> can't use it



# Scrape Miami's Bulletin for ISA

```{r}
# checking whether we are allowed to scrape this info
# This was done above and found to be TRUE

# I will load the backend of the HTML into R using
# [a] rvest::read_html() | sometimes rvest::read_html_live() if the page has some dynamic content
# [b] in some cases, we will craft this as a request as shown in slides httr2::request() > .... > httr2::resp_body_html()
isa_courses_in_r = rvest::read_html("https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/") # returns an HTML document

# we will extract the course titles, which we can do in a single pipeline
# given that they look the same on the rendered web page in Chrome
# (bolded, same font size and same font type)

# CSS selector was obtained by:
# [a] highlighting what we wanted to pull (ISA 401 course title) in Chrome -> right click
#  inspect -> right click > copy -> copy selector
# [b] from this specific example, we were able to get just the title for ISA 401
# because we had `:nth-child(24)` -> if you were to drop it --> you get all the course titles
isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("#sc_sccoursedescs > div > p.courseblocktitle > strong") |> # returns matching elements
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_titles
  
# course descriptions [using selector gadget, which does not always work]
# but when it works it is easier

isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements(".courseblockdesc") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_desc

df = data.frame(title = isa_titles, description = isa_desc)
```


Selectors:
#: select an element by its ID (#sc_sccoursedescs)
.: select elements by their class (.courseblockdesc)
no symbol: select by HTML tag name (p, strong, div)
Space: find a descendant at any depth (div strong)
>: find a direct child (div > p)
div: every <div>
div, p: every div and every p
div p: every p inside a div, at any depth
div > p: every p directly inside a div (one level)
div + p: the p right after a div, same parent
div ~ every p after a div, same parent
.parent: every element with class = "parent"
div.parent: every div with class parent
.child.rebel: elements with both classes, child and rebel
.parent .rebel: class rebel inside an element with class parent
#p1: element with id="p1"


example:
#sc_sccoursedescs > div > p.courseblocktitle > strong
1. find the element with this specific ID
2. within that element, find the direct child that is a div
3. within that div, find a direct child that is a div
4. Within that paragraph, find its direct child strong element.

but can do .courseblockdesc
- if each course decscription has that class, you don't need to specify all parent elements


Extract:
after read_html and html_elements, can do either:
  rvest::html_table() - returns a list of data frame; when webpage contains an HTML table with rows and columns
  rvest::html_text2() - character vector of text;
  rvest::html_attr("href") - character vector of attribute values
  


# wikipedia example

```{r}
wiki_url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_RedHawks_football"

robotstxt::paths_allowed(paths = "/wiki/Miami_RedHawks_football",
                         domain = "en.wikipedia.org", bot = "*")

wiki_page = httr2::request(wiki_url) |>
  httr2::req_user_agent("ISA 401 class scraper (your_email@miamioh.edu)") |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_html()

wiki_tables = wiki_page |>
  rvest::html_elements("table.wikitable") |>
  rvest::html_table()

length(wiki_tables)

bowl_games = wiki_tables[[4]]
bowl_games
```
